question: Which part of the clavicle is most commonly fractured, and to which Allman Group does it belong?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Medial third fractures are rare (<5%) and belong to Allman Group III.
Correct. The middle third is the narrowest and least protected segment, accounting for ~80% of clavicle fractures and classified as Allman Group I.
Lateral third fractures (Allman Group II, further classified by Neer) account for ~15% and carry higher non-union risk, but are not the most common site.
Allman Group I refers to the middle third, not the medial third.

overallFeedback.feedback: The clavicle's middle third — the narrowest, most exposed segment — fractures most often. This is Allman Group I.
Well done. Mid-shaft (Allman Group I) fractures dominate because the middle third lacks the ligamentous protection present at either end.
